_meta.purpose: Location-aware shopping substitutes for The Cape Table. Keyed by the exact ingredient-name text as it appears in a recipe's Shop tab (before the quantity). Looked up by the app when a visitor's stored country has an entry below.

status_meanings.native: Already a native/mainstream product in that country -- nothing to substitute, buy it as named.
status_meanings.specialty: The real South African product is orderable there, usually via a specialty importer -- an everyday supermarket alternative is also given for anyone who'd rather not order in.
status_meanings.everyday: An ordinary South African supermarket brand with no import route researched -- only a normal local-shelf equivalent is given.

_meta.note: Built 2026-08-28 from the 7 live Cape Table recipes. United Kingdom was the initial pilot; United States, Australia, New Zealand and Germany were added the same day, each researched separately. Reviewed by Koot before being wired into the app. South Africa itself needs no entries -- every ingredient is already native there.

uk.note: Orderable from South African specialty shops in the UK (e.g. Best Biltong, Weston Biltong Company). Everyday alternative: Lea & Perrins -- the standard UK Worcestershire sauce.

us.note: Sold by Welkom USA and Aubergine Foods, US-based South African grocery importers. Everyday alternative: Lea & Perrins -- the standard US Worcestershire sauce, in every supermarket.

au.note: Orderable from South African specialty shops such as Biltong & Boerewors (biltongandboerewors.com.au), which stocks the 250ml and 500ml bottles. Everyday alternative: Lea & Perrins -- the standard Worcestershire sauce on Coles and Woolworths shelves.

nz.note: Orderable from South African specialty shops in NZ -- Something From Home stocks Maggi Lazenby Worcestershire Sauce directly in 500ml and 5L. Everyday alternative: Lea & Perrins, the standard Worcestershire sauce on New Zealand supermarket shelves.

de.note: Maggi is a huge brand in Germany, but German Maggi doesn't sell this Worcester sauce -- Maggi Würze is a completely different seasoning sauce, not Worcestershire. The real substitute is itself mainstream in Germany: Lea & Perrins Worcestershire sauce is stocked directly by REWE (shop.rewe.de) and widely on Amazon.de and Kaufland, sold as "Worcestersauce".

au.note: Robertsons' spice range is stocked by South African grocers such as The South African Shop. Everyday alternative: any ground black pepper.

nz.note: Part of the Robertsons range at Something From Home. Everyday alternative: any ground black pepper, e.g. Gregg's, or a fresh peppermill.

de.note: Ordinary German schwarzer Pfeffer, whole or ground, any brand.

uk.note: Any whole cloves, e.g. Schwartz.

us.note: The Robertson's spice range is sold by Aubergine Foods and Welkom USA. Everyday alternative: McCormick whole cloves -- "naeltjies" is simply Afrikaans for cloves, no different product involved.

au.note: Robertsons' spice range is stocked by South African grocers such as The South African Shop. Everyday alternative: whole cloves from the Coles/Woolworths spice aisle.

nz.note: Robertsons spices are sold by Something From Home. Everyday alternative: whole cloves from any supermarket spice brand, e.g. Gregg's.

de.note: German ganze Gewürznelken (whole cloves), sold in every supermarket's spice aisle.

uk.note: Any Chinese five spice blend, e.g. Schwartz.

us.note: No confirmed US import route for this brand (it's distributed mainly in the UK, Canada, and Australia) -- but there's no need for one: Chinese five-spice powder is a standard US spice-aisle item, e.g. McCormick Gourmet Organic Chinese Five Spice, or available at any Asian grocery store.

au.note: Cape Herb & Spice has an official exclusive Australian distributor, Rex Imports Australia, plus stockists such as The South African Shop. Everyday alternative: any Chinese five-spice powder from the Coles/Woolworths Asian aisle.

nz.note: Cape Herb & Spice products (Cape Malay Curry, Madras Curry Seasoning) are sold by SA Shop NZ. Everyday alternative: a Chinese five spice blend, e.g. Gregg's or SpicenEasy NZ.

de.note: German Chinesisches Fünf-Gewürze-Pulver (five-spice powder), found in the spice aisle (Ostmann) or at any Asia-Laden.

uk.note: Any whole coriander seed, e.g. Schwartz.

us.note: Whole coriander seed is a standard spice-aisle item in any US supermarket, e.g. McCormick, or buy loose from a bulk-spice bin.

au.note: No Australian importer found for the Atlas brand -- use any whole coriander seed, e.g. Herbie's Spices or a supermarket own-brand.

nz.note: No NZ import route found for this South African brand. Use whole coriander seed from any supermarket spice brand or an Asian grocer's bulk bins.

de.note: German ganze Koriandersamen (whole coriander seed), a spice-aisle staple, any brand.

uk.note: Any pure MSG -- Ajinomoto is the globally recognised brand, sold in the UK especially at Asian grocers.

us.note: The Freddy Hirsch line is sold by Aubergine Foods. Everyday alternative: plain MSG is sold in mainstream US supermarkets as Ac'cent Flavor Enhancer.

au.note: Freddy Hirsch is an established import brand for Australian biltong/butchery suppliers (e.g. Biltong & Boerewors, The Casing Boutique), though their plain MSG line specifically may need ordering from freddyhirsch.co.za. Everyday alternative: any MSG, e.g. Aji-no-Moto from an Asian grocer -- or simply omit, as it's optional.

nz.note: Freddy Hirsch's biltong/braai spice range is sold by Something From Home, but plain MSG specifically isn't confirmed there. This ingredient is optional -- if using, Ajinomoto-brand MSG is available at NZ Asian grocers.

de.note: MSG (Mononatriumglutamat/E621) isn't a South African-only item -- the standard global brand Ajinomoto is sold via Asia-Läden, specialty stores like villagefoods.de, and Amazon.de/eBay.

uk.note: Any large eggs.

us.note: Fresh eggs don't ship -- any large eggs from a US supermarket, store brand or a national brand like Eggland's Best, work fine.

au.note: Fresh eggs don't travel -- use any large free-range eggs from Coles/Woolworths.

nz.note: Nulaid is a South African-only brand with no NZ presence. Use any large eggs from the supermarket, e.g. Zeagold or Woodland -- New Zealand's own major egg brands.

de.note: Ordinary German Eier Größe L (size L/large eggs), any brand from the supermarket egg shelf.

uk.note: Sago pearls aren't brand-specific -- usually found in the world-foods aisle or an Asian grocer.

us.note: Sold directly by Aubergine Foods. Everyday alternative: small pearl tapioca (not the large boba-style pearls), e.g. Bob's Red Mill Tapioca Pearls, or from an Asian grocery store.

au.note: No Australian importer found for the Imbo brand -- use sago or tapioca pearls from an Asian grocer.

nz.note: No NZ import route found for this South African brand. Use any sago or tapioca pearls, available in the baking aisle or at Asian grocers.

de.note: German Perlsago (e.g. Müllers Mühle, found at Kaufland and similar) or tapioca pearls from an Asia-Laden -- either works as a sago substitute.

uk.note: Brown & Polson -- the standard UK cornflour brand.

us.note: Sold directly by Aubergine Foods. Everyday alternative: cornstarch -- the US calls it cornstarch, not cornflour -- e.g. Argo, the standard US brand.

au.note: Stocked by several South African grocers in Australia, e.g. The South African Shop and GS International Groceries. Note: unlike in the US, Australian "cornflour" already means cornstarch, so no relabelling is needed -- White Wings Cornflour is the everyday alternative.

nz.note: Directly confirmed: Maizena Corn Flour 500g is sold by Something From Home. Everyday alternative: Edmonds Fielders Cornflour -- New Zealand's classic cornflour brand.

de.note: Maizena is itself a mainstream German brand (Unilever) -- sold everywhere as "Maizena Feine Speisestärke". Buy it as named, nothing to substitute.

uk.note: Brown & Polson -- the standard UK cornflour brand.

us.note: Sold directly by Aubergine Foods. Everyday alternative: any US cornstarch, e.g. Argo, the standard brand -- this is the same product, just called cornflour in South Africa.

au.note: Stocked by several South African grocers in Australia, e.g. The South African Shop and GS International Groceries. Note: Australian "cornflour" already means cornstarch (same as in South Africa), so no relabelling is needed -- White Wings Cornflour is the everyday alternative.

nz.note: Directly confirmed: Maizena Corn Flour 500g is sold by Something From Home. In NZ, "cornflour" already means cornstarch, so no renaming needed. Everyday alternative: Edmonds Fielders Cornflour.

de.note: Maizena is itself a mainstream German brand (Unilever) -- sold everywhere as "Maizena Feine Speisestärke". Buy it as named, nothing to substitute.

uk.note: Any pure vanilla extract, e.g. Nielsen-Massey.

us.note: No confirmed US import route for this brand -- but "Bourbon" vanilla is a familiar US term too (it refers to Madagascar/Bourbon Islands origin, not the whiskey), so any pure vanilla extract works, e.g. Nielsen-Massey Madagascar Bourbon Vanilla Extract or McCormick pure vanilla extract.

au.note: No Australian importer found for this South African brand -- use any pure vanilla extract, e.g. Queen (an Australian brand, widely at Coles/Woolworths).

nz.note: No NZ import route found for this South African brand. Use any pure vanilla extract, e.g. Heilala -- a well-regarded NZ/Pacific vanilla brand -- or Queen.

de.note: Pure Bourbon vanilla extract isn't a standard German shelf item -- German baking mostly uses Vanillezucker (vanilla sugar) instead. For the real thing, Nielsen-Massey Madagascar Bourbon Vanilla Extract is available via specialty baking shops (e.g. ryan-s.de) and Amazon.de.

uk.note: Any full-egg mayonnaise -- Hellmann's is the closest widely-available match in richness.

us.note: Sold directly by Aubergine Foods. Everyday alternative: Hellmann's (called Best Foods west of the Rockies) Real Mayonnaise -- a genuine egg-based mayonnaise, as opposed to Miracle Whip, which actually is labeled "salad dressing" on US shelves, so the same distinction applies here.

au.note: Stocked by South African grocers in Australia, e.g. The South African Shop and South African Home Foods. Everyday alternative: a whole-egg mayonnaise such as Praise Whole Egg Mayonnaise, not a lighter "salad dressing" style.

nz.note: Strongly available -- Nola Mayonnaise is sold by Something From Home, SA Shop NZ, International Sweets NZ and Elite Meats Hamilton. Everyday alternative: Best Foods Real Mayonnaise (made with whole egg), not a lighter "salad dressing" style.

de.note: Look for a product labelled "Mayonnaise" (not "Salatcreme" or "Salatmayonnaise", which are lower-fat dressings) -- e.g. Thomy Delikatess-Mayonnaise or Kühne, both real egg-yolk mayonnaise and widely stocked.

uk.note: Any baby gherkins or dill pickles, supermarket own-brand is fine.

us.note: No confirmed South African import route found for this brand -- small tart gherkins/cornichons and dill pickles are both easy US supermarket items: Mt. Olive baby gherkins or cornichons for the gherkin option, Vlasic or Claussen for dill pickles.

au.note: No Australian importer found for the Rhodes brand -- use any baby gherkins or dill pickles, e.g. Masterfoods or a supermarket own-brand.

nz.note: No NZ import route found for Rhodes specifically. Use any jarred baby gherkins or dill pickles from the supermarket pickle aisle, e.g. Craig's or Always Fresh.

de.note: Kühne is the classic German brand for this -- their Gewürzgurken (baby pickled gherkins) or Senfgurken/Dillgurken (mustard/dill pickles) are in every supermarket.

uk.note: Any raw or clear honey.

us.note: No confirmed import route for this brand -- any raw or local honey works, e.g. Nature Nate's Raw Honey (a similarly named US brand, unrelated) or a local farmers'-market honey.

au.note: No Australian importer found for this South African brand -- use any raw or local honey, e.g. Capilano.

nz.note: No NZ import route found for this South African brand. New Zealand has its own excellent raw and manuka honey producers -- any local raw honey, e.g. Arataki or Airborne, works well.

de.note: Ordinary raw/unfiltered honey, e.g. a Bio-Rohhonig from Alnatura or Breitsamer, found in the Bio aisle, a Reformhaus, or DM drugstore.

uk.note: Any toasted sesame oil, e.g. Clearspring or an Asian grocer's own-brand.

us.note: No confirmed import route for this brand -- any toasted sesame oil, e.g. Kadoya or La Tourangelle, sold in the international aisle of most US supermarkets or at any Asian grocery store.

au.note: No Australian importer found for this South African brand -- use any toasted or pure sesame oil, e.g. Chang's, from the Coles/Woolworths Asian aisle.

nz.note: No NZ import route found for this South African brand. Use any pure or toasted sesame oil, e.g. Lee Kum Kee or Chang's, from the supermarket or an Asian grocer.

de.note: Toasted sesame oil (geröstetes Sesamöl) is a standard Asia-Laden item in German cities, and also on Amazon.de -- any brand works.

uk.note: Any long-grain white rice, e.g. Tilda.

us.note: Sold directly by Aubergine Foods as "Tastic Long Grain Parboiled Rice." Everyday alternative: since Tastic is a parboiled ("easy-cook") rice, the closest US match is a parboiled rice like Uncle Ben's Original Converted Rice, though any plain long-grain white rice such as Mahatma or Carolina also works.

au.note: Sold into Australia rebranded as "Protea Rice" by South African grocers such as Springbok Delights and South African Home Foods. Everyday alternative: any long-grain white rice, e.g. SunRice.

nz.note: Directly confirmed -- several Tastic rice varieties are sold by Something From Home. Everyday alternative: SunRice long-grain white rice, or a supermarket own-brand.

de.note: Ordinary German long-grain white rice (Langkornreis), e.g. Oryza, Uncle Ben's or a supermarket own-brand.

uk.note: This recipe offers two smoking methods, both easy in the UK: wood chips for a smoker/BBQ are widely sold there (hardware shops, Amazon, BBQ suppliers); for the stovetop-in-a-pot method, use any long-grain rice in place of Tastic rice, any light or dark brown sugar (e.g. Tate & Lyle) in place of Huletts brown sugar, and any UK black tea (e.g. PG Tips or Yorkshire Tea) in place of Joko tea.

us.note: For a smoker or grill: wood chips are trivially available at any US hardware store, Walmart, or Amazon (e.g. Weber or Kingsford). For the stovetop method: any US long-grain rice (Mahatma, Carolina), light or dark brown sugar (Domino, C&H), and a plain black tea -- Lipton black tea bags, torn open, are the easiest everyday stand-in for Joko.

au.note: For a smoker or kettle BBQ: wood chips are sold at hardware/BBQ shops such as Bunnings (Heat Beads, Matador). For the stovetop method: any long-grain rice (or the Tastic-rebrand "Protea Rice" from a South African grocer), any brown sugar, and any black tea bags (Joko itself is stocked by The South African Shop) all work.

nz.note: For a smoker/BBQ: wood chips, including native manuka, are easy to find at Mitre 10 and Bunnings NZ. For the stovetop method: Tastic rice is sold by Something From Home (or sub SunRice), Joko Tea is also stocked there, and Huletts brown sugar can be swapped for Chelsea Brown Sugar.

de.note: For a smoker/BBQ: wood chips (Räucherchips) are widely sold at OBI, Hornbach and Amazon.de (e.g. Weber or Mr. BBQ brand). For the stovetop method: German long-grain rice, brauner Zucker (brown sugar, any brand), and a black tea such as Meßmer, a mainstream German brand.
